examples.ko: 교실 뒤에서 친구들이 쑥덕쑥덕 이야기하고 있어요.
examples.en: My friends are whispering at the back of the classroom.

examples.ko: 제가 들어가자 사람들이 쑥덕쑥덕 말하다가 갑자기 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: When I walked in, people were whispering and then suddenly went quiet.
The neighborhood ladies are whispering rumors to each other.
What are you two whispering about so secretly?

examples.ko: 회의 중에 뒤에서 쑥덕쑥덕하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear whispering from behind during the meeting.

examples.ko: 아이들이 선물을 숨기고 쑥덕쑥덕 작전을 짜요.
examples.en: The kids hide the present and whisper as they plan their scheme.

explain: 남이 들으면 안 되는 이야기나 소문, 흉을 작은 소리로 주고받는 느낌이 있어요. '속닥속닥', '수군수군'과 비슷하게 쓰는데, 뒷말하는 분위기일 때 특히 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of exchanging quiet talk, rumors or gossip that others shouldn't hear. It is close to '속닥속닥' and '수군수군', and fits especially well when the mood is one of talking behind someone's back.

examples.en: The hospital said I have a stone in my gallbladder.

examples.ko: 쓸개 수술을 받고 일주일 동안 입원했어요.
examples.en: I had gallbladder surgery and stayed in the hospital for a week.

examples.ko: 기름진 음식을 많이 먹으면 쓸개가 힘들어해요.
examples.en: Eating a lot of greasy food puts a strain on your gallbladder.
The gallbladder is attached under the liver.

examples.ko: 쓸개즙은 기름진 음식을 소화하는 데 도움을 줘요.
examples.en: Bile helps digest fatty food.

examples.ko: 쓸개를 떼어 내도 일상생활은 할 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard you can live normally even after the gallbladder is removed.

explain: 병원에서는 보통 '담낭'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 '쓸개'라고 해요. 간 아래에 붙어서 쓸개즙을 모아 두는 기관이고, '쓸개 빠진 사람' 같은 관용 표현에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 상사 앞에서 쓸개가 빠진 사람처럼 굴지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't act like you have no backbone in front of your boss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자존심이나 줏대 없이 남에게 비굴하게 구는 사람을 흉볼 때 써요. '쓸개 빠진 사람'처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone who acts servile, with no pride or backbone. Often said as '쓸개 빠진 사람'.

phrases.example: 이익에 따라 간에 붙었다 쓸개에 붙었다 하는 사람은 믿기 어려워요.
phrases.en: It is hard to trust someone who switches sides depending on their own interest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 이익에 따라 이쪽저쪽에 붙으며 태도를 바꾸는 사람을 비난하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A criticism of someone who changes sides back and forth to suit their own interest.

explain_en: Hospitals usually say '담낭', while everyday speech uses '쓸개'. It is the organ under the liver that stores bile, and it also appears in idioms like '쓸개 빠진 사람'.

en: be swept; be washed away; be rubbed raw

examples.en: The fallen leaves were swept by the wind and gathered on one side.

examples.ko: 파도에 쓸려 온 쓰레기가 해변에 가득해요.
examples.en: The beach is full of trash washed in by the waves.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 흙이 다 쓸려 내려갔어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so all the soil was washed away.
My heel hurts because the new shoes rubbed it raw.

examples.ko: 물살에 쓸리지 않게 제 손을 꼭 잡으세요.
examples.en: Hold my hand tightly so you aren't swept away by the current.

examples.ko: 눈이 깨끗이 쓸린 길로 천천히 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly along the road where the snow had been swept clean.

explain: '쓸다'의 피동으로, 바람이나 물에 밀려가는 것 또는 살갗이 스쳐 아픈 것에 써요. 감정이나 분위기에 끌려가는 것은 '휩쓸리다'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '쓸다', used for things pushed along by wind or water, or skin that gets scraped. For being carried away by emotion or the mood, people often say '휩쓸리다' instead.

examples.ko: 놀란 엄마가 아이를 안고 가슴을 쓸어내렸어요.
examples.en: The startled mother held her child and patted her own chest to calm down.

examples.ko: 할머니가 제 머리를 부드럽게 쓸어내려 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother gently stroked my hair down for me.
I smooth the wrinkles of my clothes down with my hand.

examples.ko: 다행히 아무도 안 다쳐서 가슴을 쓸어내리고 있어요.
examples.en: Luckily nobody was hurt, so I'm relieved and calming myself.
He laughed while stroking down his long beard.

examples.ko: 아이 등을 쓸어내리면 기침이 좀 가라앉아요.
examples.en: If you stroke the child's back downward, the cough settles a bit.

explain: 손바닥으로 위에서 아래로 천천히 문지르는 동작이에요. 몸의 부분이나 옷, 수염처럼 눈에 보이는 대상에 쓰고, '가슴을 쓸어내리다'는 안도할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.example: 합격 소식을 듣고 그제야 가슴을 쓸어내렸어요.
phrases.en: Only after hearing I had passed did I finally breathe easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 걱정했던 일이 잘 끝나서 안심할 때 써요. 실제로 가슴을 만지지 않아도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you feel relieved that something you worried about turned out fine. You don't have to actually touch your chest.
phrases.en_equiv: to breathe a sigh of relief

explain_en: It describes slowly rubbing downward with the palm. It is used for visible things like body parts, clothes or a beard, and '가슴을 쓸어내리다' is an expression for feeling relieved.

examples.en: He nodded with a bitter smile.
After hearing my friend's words, I turned away with a bitter feeling.
I sighed bitterly when I saw the result.
My father just looked out the window with a bitter expression.

examples.ko: 그 소식에 씁쓸히 웃을 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.en: I could only give a bitter smile at the news.
The way he spoke so bitterly stays on my mind.

explain: '씁쓸하다'의 부사형으로, 서운하거나 허탈한 마음으로 하는 행동 앞에 와요. '씁쓸히 웃다'가 가장 잘 어울리고, 말할 때는 '씁쓸하게'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: This is the adverb form of '씁쓸하다', placed before actions done with a hurt or hollow feeling. '씁쓸히 웃다' is the most natural pairing, and in speech '씁쓸하게' is also common.

examples.ko: 동생이 화가 나서 씩씩대며 방으로 들어갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling got angry and went into the room, huffing.
Why are you huffing and puffing like that?
I ran up the stairs and I'm panting.

examples.ko: 그는 한참을 씩씩댔지만 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: He huffed for a long while but couldn't say anything.
Stop huffing, sit down and let's talk calmly.
The child huffing in frustration looked cute.

explain: 화가 나거나 힘들어서 숨을 거칠게 쉬는 모습이에요. '씩씩거리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. '씩씩하다'(용감하고 활기차다)와는 전혀 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It describes breathing roughly because you are angry or exhausted. '씩씩거리다' is also used with the same meaning. It is a completely different word from '씩씩하다' (brave and lively), so don't mix them up.

examples.en: My lips twitch because I'm holding back a laugh.

examples.ko: 화가 나자 그의 눈썹이 씰룩거리기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When he got angry, his eyebrow started to twitch.
She laughed, twitching the corners of her mouth.
The kid wiggling his bottom is cute.
The puppy sniffed, twitching its nose.

examples.ko: 얼굴 근육이 씰룩거리지 않게 꾹 참았어요.
examples.en: I held on tight so my face muscles wouldn't twitch.

explain: '떨다'보다 근육이 작게 반복해서 움직이는 느낌이고, 입·눈썹·코·엉덩이처럼 몸의 한 부분이 움직일 때 어울려요. 참느라 저절로 움직일 때도, 일부러 흔들 때도 써요. '씰룩대다'도 비슷해요.
explain_en: Compared with '떨다' (to tremble), it feels like a muscle moving in small, repeated jerks, and it fits a single body part such as the mouth, eyebrow, nose or bottom. It works for involuntary movement while holding something back and for wiggling on purpose. '씰룩대다' is similar.

examples.ko: 아이가 입을 씰룩씰룩 움직이며 울음을 참았어요.
examples.en: The child held back tears, twitching his mouth.
The rabbit whose nose keeps twitching is cute.
My shoulders shake as I hold back laughter.
His eyebrow twitched over and over.
She walks away wiggling her bottom.

examples.ko: 입꼬리가 씰룩씰룩 올라가는 걸 숨기지 못했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't hide my mouth corners twitching upward.

explain: 몸의 한 부분이 작게 반복해서 움직이는 모양을 나타내요. 보통 '씰룩거리다'와 같이 입, 코, 눈썹, 어깨 같은 말과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It shows a body part moving in small, repeated jerks. Like '씰룩거리다', it usually goes with words such as mouth, nose, eyebrow or shoulders.

examples.en: The brothers got into a fierce fight over the inheritance.

examples.ko: 사람들이 세일 상품을 두고 아귀다툼을 해요.
examples.en: People scramble and fight over the sale items.
The parents are worn out by the brothers' squabbling.
A scramble broke out to grab the cramped seats.

examples.ko: 아귀다툼 끝에 결국 둘 다 빈손으로 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: After all the squabbling, both of them went home empty-handed.

examples.ko: 회사 안에서 아귀다툼하는 모습이 보기 싫어요.
examples.en: I hate seeing people scrapping with each other at the company.

explain: 서로 이기거나 더 가지려고 욕심내며 몰아붙이는 싸움이에요. 그냥 '싸움'보다 이익을 두고 보기 안 좋게 다툰다는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '아귀다툼을 벌이다/하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It is a fight where people greedily push to win or grab more. Compared with plain '싸움', it strongly suggests an unattractive struggle over gain. It is usually used as '아귀다툼을 벌이다/하다'.

examples.ko: 잘난 척하는 모습이 아니꼬워서 보기 싫어요.
examples.en: His showing off is so irritating that I can't stand to look.
The way that person talks is really obnoxious.

examples.ko: 돈 좀 있다고 자랑하는 게 아니꼽게 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: His bragging about having some money felt sickening.
He looked at me with a snooty expression.
Even though I found it distasteful, I held back.

examples.ko: 상사의 행동이 아니꼬웠지만 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: My boss's behavior galled me, but I said nothing.

explain: 잘난 척하거나 거만한 모습을 보고 비위가 상할 때 써요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '아니꼬워요', '아니꼬운'으로 바뀌어요. 일상에서는 '재수 없다', '꼴사납다'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone's showing off or arrogance turns your stomach. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it becomes '아니꼬워요' and '아니꼬운'. In casual talk people also say things like '재수 없다' or '꼴사납다'.

examples.ko: 제가 너무 아둔해서 그 뜻을 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was so slow that I didn't understand what it meant.
He may seem dull, but he is a diligent person.
Thank you for teaching someone as slow as me.
I was foolish to be fooled so easily.
It feels bad to be called dull-witted.
He isn't dull-witted, yet he has no confidence.

explain: 머리 회전이 느리고 눈치가 둔하다는 뜻이라 남에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 그래서 '제가 아둔해서'처럼 자신을 낮출 때 많이 써요. '우둔하다'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: It means slow in thought and dull at picking up on things, so using it about others can be rude. That is why people often use it to humble themselves, as in '제가 아둔해서'. It is similar to '우둔하다'.

examples.ko: 매달 생활비를 벌려고 아등바등 살고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm struggling hard every month just to earn living expenses.
Even though I struggle so hard, my salary stays the same.
You don't have to struggle so desperately.
Many mothers are struggling hard to raise their kids.

examples.ko: 그는 집을 사려고 아등바등 돈을 모았어요.
examples.en: He scrimped and saved desperately to buy a house.
The two fought tooth and nail to beat each other.

explain: 힘든 상황에서 어떻게든 애쓰는 모습이에요. 보는 사람이 안쓰럽거나 지치게 느끼는 분위기가 있어서 '아등바등 살다'처럼 많이 말해요. '열심히'보다 더 힘겹게 버티는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It shows someone straining to get by in a difficult situation. It often carries a sense of pity or weariness, as in '아등바등 살다'. Compared with '열심히', it feels more like hanging on with great effort.

en: paying no heed; having no concern with

examples.ko: 그는 남들 시선에 아랑곳없이 큰 소리로 노래했어요.
examples.en: He sang loudly, paying no mind to others' stares.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 것에 아랑곳없이 아이들이 뛰어놀아요.
examples.en: The kids run around playing, unbothered by the rain.

examples.ko: 주변 사람이 뭐라고 하든 저는 아랑곳없어요.
examples.en: I don't care what the people around me say.
I envy his attitude of not caring what others say.

examples.ko: 추위에 아랑곳없이 사람들이 줄을 서 있었어요.
examples.en: People stood in line, regardless of the cold.
No matter how much we tried to stop him, he paid no heed.

explain: 대부분 '~에 아랑곳없이'처럼 쓰고, '~에 아랑곳하지 않고'라고도 해요. 주변 시선이나 날씨, 충고를 신경 쓰지 않고 자기 할 일을 계속하는 모습에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '~에 아랑곳없이', and you can also say '~에 아랑곳하지 않고'. It fits someone who keeps doing their own thing without minding stares, weather or advice.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 살던 집이 아련히 떠올라요.
examples.en: The house I lived in as a child comes faintly to mind.
A bell could be heard faintly from far away.
There is one song I remember dimly.
The mountain looked hazy in the fog.
I vaguely and wistfully recall my first love's face.

examples.ko: 아련히 남아 있는 그날의 냄새가 그리워요.
examples.en: I miss the faint scent of that day that still lingers.

explain: 또렷하지 않게 멀고 희미한데, 그리운 마음이 함께 들어 있어요. '희미하게'는 단순히 흐린 것이고, '아련히'는 추억이나 소리에 감정이 담길 때 잘 어울려요. 형용사 '아련하다'는 '아련한 추억'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means faint and far away, with a touch of longing mixed in. '희미하게' just means unclear, while '아련히' suits memories and sounds that carry emotion. The adjective '아련하다' is used as in '아련한 추억'.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 유명한 작품의 아류라는 평을 받았어요.
examples.en: That movie was criticized as a knockoff of a famous work.

examples.ko: 아류 소리를 듣지 않으려면 나만의 색이 필요해요.
examples.en: To avoid being called a copycat, you need your own style.

examples.ko: 이 가수는 선배 가수의 아류로 보이기 싫어해요.
examples.en: This singer doesn't want to be seen as an imitation of a senior singer.

examples.ko: 유행하던 게임의 아류가 너무 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Far too many knockoffs of the trendy game came out.
The director was upset by criticism that the film was derivative.

examples.ko: 처음엔 아류였지만 지금은 독자적인 스타일을 만들었어요.
examples.en: He started out as an imitator, but now he has made his own style.

explain: 독창성 없이 다른 유명한 것을 따라 한 사람이나 작품을 낮춰 말할 때 써요. 작품에는 '아류작'이라고도 하고, 칭찬으로는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used to disparage a person or work that follows a famous original without being original. For works you can also say '아류작', and it is never a compliment.

examples.ko: 눈을 감으면 그 사람 얼굴이 아른거려요.
examples.en: When I close my eyes, that person's face flickers before me.
The ripples shimmering in the sunlight look pretty.
I was tired, so the letters kept swimming before my eyes.

examples.ko: 먹고 싶던 케이크가 눈앞에 아른거려서 참기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The cake I wanted keeps floating before my eyes, so it's hard to resist.

examples.ko: 아이의 웃는 얼굴이 머릿속에서 계속 아른거릴 거예요.
examples.en: The child's smiling face will keep flickering in my mind.

examples.ko: 더운 길 위로 아지랑이가 아른거리고 있어요.
examples.en: Heat haze is shimmering above the hot road.

explain: '떠오르다'는 생각이 한 번 나는 것이고, '아른거리다'는 흐릿한 모습이 자꾸 보였다 사라지는 느낌이에요. '눈에 아른거리다', '얼굴이 아른거리다'처럼 쓰고, '아른대다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: '떠오르다' is a thought coming to mind once, while '아른거리다' feels like a blurry image that keeps appearing and fading. It is used as in '눈에 아른거리다' or '얼굴이 아른거리다', and you can also say '아른대다'.

examples.ko: 눈만 감으면 고향 집이 아른아른 보여요.
examples.en: Whenever I close my eyes, my hometown house appears hazily.

examples.ko: 더운 길 위에서 아지랑이가 아른아른 피어올라요.
examples.en: Heat haze shimmers up from the hot road.
Moonlight shimmers on the water.

examples.ko: 그 장면이 자꾸 머릿속에 아른아른 떠올라요.
examples.en: That scene keeps flickering in my mind.
I was sleepy, so the letters looked wavy.
The lights wavered and faded into the distance.

explain: 흐릿한 모습이 가볍게 흔들리듯 보이는 모양이에요. 보통 '보이다', '떠오르다', '비치다' 같은 말과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It shows a blurry image appearing to waver lightly. It usually pairs with verbs like '보이다', '떠오르다' and '비치다'.

examples.ko: 아메바는 현미경으로 봐야 보이는 작은 생물이에요.
examples.en: An amoeba is a tiny organism you can only see under a microscope.
We observed an amoeba in science class.
The amoeba moves while constantly changing shape.
Amoebas live even in the water of a small puddle.

examples.ko: 아메바처럼 몸이 하나의 세포인 생물이 있어요.
examples.en: There are organisms whose body is a single cell, like the amoeba.
The amoeba's movement was so fascinating that I watched it for a long time.

explain: 주로 과학 시간이나 책에서 만나는 말이에요. 몸이 세포 하나로 이루어진 '단세포 생물'의 대표적인 예로 많이 들어요.
explain_en: You mostly meet this word in science class or books. It is often given as a typical example of a '단세포 생물' (single-celled organism).

examples.ko: 아무러면 싼 옷이 비싼 옷만큼 튼튼하겠어요?
examples.en: Surely a cheap coat can't be as sturdy as an expensive one, right?

examples.ko: 아무러면 처음 하는 사람이 전문가만큼 잘하겠어요?
examples.en: Surely a beginner can't do as well as an expert, can they?
Surely I wouldn't have deceived my friend, would I?
Surely that person wouldn't have lied, would he?

examples.ko: 아무러면 하루 만에 다 배울 수 있겠어요?
examples.en: Surely you can't learn it all in one day, can you?
Surely my parents must understand how I feel, don't they?

explain: 뒤에 '-겠어요?' 같은 반문이 와서 '설마 그럴 리 있겠어요?'라는 뜻을 나타내요. 예스러운 느낌이 있어서 일상 대화에서는 '설마', '아무리 그래도'처럼 말하는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: It is followed by a rhetorical question like '-겠어요?' to mean 'How could that possibly be?'. It sounds a bit old-fashioned, so in daily talk many people say '설마' or '아무리 그래도' instead.
